notes: EPT (mayfly/stonefly/caddisfly) taxa richness; more sensitive taxa indicate better condition.
Percent tolerant individuals; a higher share of pollution-tolerant taxa indicates worse condition.
Chlorophyll a; higher indicates algal enrichment/eutrophication (worse).
pH degrades condition at BOTH extremes. Two-sided (optimum) curve: scored 1.0 across the reference interquartile core, falling in both tails.
Turbidity; higher indicates more suspended sediment (worse).

Percent of native fish individuals that are simple lithophils, spawning on clean coarse substrate without nest building; higher is better. Reproduction depends on substrate that fine sediment smothers.

Native non-tolerant fish taxa richness (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is better. Total richness need not fall under disturbance, because tolerant species replace intolerant ones; this counts only the taxa that do not tolerate it.
Percent of native fish taxa not classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is better. A proportion, so it does not carry the size of a region's species pool the way a richness count does.
Percent of native fish individuals classed tolerant (TOLERANCE_NRSA); higher is worse. Dominance by tolerant fish is a standard multimetric-index component of disturbance.
Native fish taxa richness; higher is better.
Bankfull width-to-depth ratio; both over-widened (very high) and incised (very low) degrade condition. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.

Log relative bed stability; departure from the reference core in EITHER direction departs from reference (negative excess fines, positive an armored, sediment-starved bed, the classic below-impoundment failure). The pilot's rising direction scored armored beds 1.0 and left Sediment continuity blind to its textbook failure mode. Two-sided form is an owner decision at the adversarial review gate, 2026-08-21.
Log mean substrate diameter; coarser substrate generally better, but valley-type dependent.
Large woody debris volume per 100 m; higher is better.
Percent sand and fines; higher indicates fine-sediment loading (worse).
Channel sinuosity; higher generally indicates a more natural planform.

Mean bank angle; very steep banks indicate incision and very flat banks an over-widened, aggrading channel, so departure from the reference core in either direction departs from reference. Mean bankfull height; both incision (very high banks) and over-widening (very low) depart from reference. Two-sided curve centered on the reference core.
Mid-channel canopy density; higher shading generally better for thermal/light regime.
Riparian canopy plus mid-layer plus ground cover; higher is better.
Percent embeddedness; higher means interstitial spaces filled with fines (worse).
Natural fish cover; higher is better.

Base-flow index (% of streamflow from baseflow); a higher baseflow share indicates a more stable, groundwater-supported flow regime. referenceMethod.statement: Reference condition is set by a fixed landscape-pressure screen, never by a score. 24 borrow comparable least-disturbed stations from a wider region, stating the region and the transfer risk. 3 carry the national reference label: reference curve fitted to comparable least-disturbed stations drawn from the national pool, because this ecoregion and its parents hold too few of their own. 5 carry the published benchmark label: scored against a published criterion rather than against stations from this ecoregion. The criterion carries its own definition of reference, which need not match this assessment's. 21 rest on a flagged transfer: a comparable least-disturbed pool the recovery test did not confirm for this ecoregion, used because no validated source supports the metric here, with transfer risk unvalidated and confidence capped. A metric that no basis supports is not scored, and the function it would have scored is reported as unassessed.

insufficientReferenceSupport.statement: Insufficient reference support. No station pool, from this ecoregion's own least-disturbed streams or from a wider region under the regional screen, holds enough comparable stations with a value for this metric and passes acceptance. The local reference: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. This ecoregion under the regional screen: 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level II pool (15.4): 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The Level I pool (15): 0 usable stations, below the floor of 10. The NARS-9 pool (CPL): The curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.41 over 98 reference and 255 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). No other basis supports it either. National reference: 0 matched national donors, below the floor of 10. 763 national donors inside the comparability envelope, but the curve on this pool would rank pressured stations above reference stations (discrimination check inverted, area under the curve 0.31 over 763 reference and 2013 pressured stations), so it is refused under methodology 0.16 (owner decision D13). Modeled reference: The model registry holds no approved specification for this metric. Published benchmark: The published criteria STAF draws on include none for this metric. No curve was built and the metric is not scored.
